verdict.reasoning: Patient reports itchy, red skin for a few days: “it's been a few days now. I have like a sore and a red skin. It's… really itchy.” Duration later summarized by doctor as four days. 'Intensely' itchy is consistent with “itching a lot, like all the time… super annoying.”
Doctor summarizes: “for the last four days, you've had very itchy skin, very sore skin…” which matches rash duration of 4 days.
Distribution stated: patient: “Mostly like my chest, my… hands, my arms… just the chest, hands, and, like, inside the elbows.” This corresponds to chest, hands, and antecubital fossae.
Sleep/work impact: “I can't even sleep at night… even at work… I'm always like, disturbed by this disease.”

Soreness and cracking: “You also mentioned it's been quite sore.” Patient: “my skin is a bit cracked in some parts.” No bleeding/pus: Doctor: “have you noticed any bleeding… or discharge…?” Patient: “No… No.”

System review: Doctor asks about fever, chest, cough, breathing, bowels, urine; patient denies: “Any temperature or fevers?… No. Just the itching… No cough? No. Breathing difficulties? Patient: No… You're passing urine Okay? Patient: I think so.” GI symptoms implied okay when doctor says “your bowels are working okay.”

OTC steroid: “I bought like a steroid cream at the pharmacy last night, but it apparently didn't help.” Antihistamines: “I have tried antihistamines lately, but it didn't really help.” Both indicate minimal relief.
History: “earlier I was like prescribed for my eczema… my eczema was more like only in the arms. And now it's also on the chest and on the hands as well.”
Asthma history: “Apart from the eczema, do you have any other medical problems…?” Patient: “No, I just had asthma in the past. But not anymore?”
Medications: “And do you take any regular medications at the moment? Patient: No.”
Allergies: “Do you have any allergies at all? Patient: Oh, allergies. No.”
Living situation: “So I live with a few flatmates… I'm living with a few people to save money.”

Work: “I work at a pharmaceutical company… I'm a… like a kind of project manager.” This supports working as a project manager in pharma; wording “pharmacy” is close but core fact (pharmaceutical company, project manager) is correct.
Smoking: “do you smoke at all? Patient: No.”
Alcohol: “do you drink much…? Patient: …I'd say a few. A few beers per week. Something like this.”
Hiking limited: “I like first instance hiking during the weekend… I wanted to do that last weekend and it was super painful.” Indicates hiking habit now limited by rash-related pain/itch.

Transcript only says: “having looked at your skin, the rash does appear quite familiar” and that patient has “dry skin and some cracked skin.” It does not describe “erythematous, dry, eczematous patches on the chest, hands, and antecubital areas” as tele-exam findings.

Absence of bleeding/pus is from history: “have you noticed any bleeding… or discharge…? Patient: No.” The doctor does not state “No discharge or bleeding is noted… on tele-exam,” so attributing this specifically to exam is additional.
Assessment: “I do wonder whether this is a flare up of your eczema… you said it's quite itchy…” This supports acute eczema flare with severe pruritus.
Topical steroid: “I wonder whether giving you stronger prescription of a steroid may be beneficial, which I'm happy to prescribe to you today.”

Doctor: “I'm going to give you something, some emollients which helps to moisturize the skin to use in the bath and shower.” Frequency “twice daily and after showers” is not stated, so that part is an addition.
Antihistamine: “I can give you something a little bit stronger today as well. Something like fexofenadine, which I can give to you today. It's definitely worth trying it.”

Irritants: Doctor discusses potential triggers such as shower gels and clothing: “anything you wear or anything you use in terms of shower gels or soap. Because if that's causing your symptoms, then we need to have a discussion about that next time I see you.” This effectively counsels avoidance of irritant triggers.
Trigger diary: “it's also worth keeping a diary of any triggers which are affecting your symptoms. Anything you wear or anything you use in terms of shower gels or soap.”

Follow-up: “It's definitely worth using that for the first seven to 10 days before we make a decision on whether it's working or not… But do come back and see me next week if things don't get better.” This supports follow up in about 7–10 days or sooner if not improving/worsening.
